memories.author: patient
memories.text: Intake note (patient-reported): Owns and runs a restaurant, so works late most evenings. Eats dinner late, usually around 11 pm. Keeps the full Ramadan fasts every year. Wants advice on fitting his tablets and meals around the restaurant timings.

memories.author: D01
memories.text: Rx (continued): metformin (Glycomet) 1000 mg BD with breakfast and dinner. Glimepiride (Amaryl) 2 mg OD before breakfast. Supply 90 days.

memories.author: D01
memories.text:
S: k/c/o T2DM on metformin and glimepiride. Eats dinner late, around 11 pm, most days. Keeps Ramadan fasts. C/o mild tiredness in the mornings. No hypoglycaemia symptoms.
O: BP 124/80 mmHg, pulse 76/min, wt 86 kg. O/E: no ulcer, foot sensation normal.
A: 1. T2DM, sugar control not at target.
P: 1. Continue metformin 1000 mg BD. 2. Continue glimepiride 2 mg OD before breakfast. 3. HbA1c today.
Adv: Shift the main meal earlier in the evening; no sugary drinks; walk 30 min after dinner, 5 days a week. R/V in 3 months.

memories.author: lab
memories.text: Lab report: HbA1c (glycated haemoglobin) 8.2 % (reference below 5.7 %). Sample: venous blood, Sunrise Family Clinic.

memories.author: D01
memories.text:
S: k/c/o T2DM. Still eating late on restaurant nights, dinner often after 10.30 pm. Missed glimepiride on two days last month when busy. Passing urine more at night, no thirst. No hypoglycaemia.
O: BP 126/82 mmHg, pulse 80/min, wt 87 kg. O/E: NAD.
A: 1. T2DM, HbA1c higher than in May, adherence an issue.
P: 1. Continue metformin 1000 mg BD. 2. Continue glimepiride 2 mg OD before breakfast; set a phone alarm for it. 3. HbA1c sent today.
Adv: Keep dinner before 9 pm where possible; half plate of rice with dal and vegetables; walk after dinner. R/V in 3 months.

memories.author: lab
memories.text: Lab report: HbA1c (glycated haemoglobin) 8.6 % (reference below 5.7 %). Sample: venous blood, Sunrise Family Clinic.

memories.author: D01
memories.text:
S: k/c/o T2DM. Feels well. No previous eye check on record. No hypoglycaemia. Still working long hours.
O: BP 128/84 mmHg, pulse 78/min, wt 86 kg. O/E: NAD.
A: 1. T2DM, sugar control still above target. 2. Diabetic eye screening due.
P: 1. Continue metformin 1000 mg BD. 2. Continue glimepiride 2 mg OD before breakfast. 3. Referred to ophthalmology for diabetic eye screening; letter given to patient.
Adv: Reduce white rice to one katori per meal; add dal, sprouts and salad; walk 30 min daily. R/V in 2 months.

memories.author: D01
memories.text: Referral to ophthalmology: Dr Kamath, Narayana Nethralaya. Reason: diabetic eye screening in a patient with type 2 diabetes on metformin and glimepiride. Referred by Dr Anjali Mehta (D01) on 2025-12-09. Referral letter given to the patient.

memories.author: D01
memories.text:
S: k/c/o T2DM. Ramadan due to start in about a week; plans to keep the fasts. C/o nil hypoglycaemia. Works long hours, dinner still late.
O: BP 122/78 mmHg, pulse 74/min, wt 85 kg. O/E: NAD.
A: 1. T2DM. Fasting in Ramadan needs a change in glimepiride timing.
P: 1. Metformin 1000 mg BD, taken with suhoor and with iftar. 2. Glimepiride reduced to 1 mg OD, taken with the iftar meal for the Ramadan period only. 3. Check sugar before suhoor and 2 hours after iftar. 4. Warning signs of low sugar reviewed: shaky, sweaty, confused.
Adv: Protein-rich suhoor; avoid sweets and sweet drinks at iftar; 20 min walk after iftar. R/V in 2 months.

memories.author: D01
memories.text: Rx change: glimepiride 2 mg OD before breakfast changed to 1 mg OD with the iftar meal, for the Ramadan fasting period only. Metformin 1000 mg BD unchanged.

memories.author: D01
memories.text:
S: k/c/o T2DM. Ramadan fasts completed, most days kept. Back to routine. C/o tiredness after lunch. No hypoglycaemia during the fasting month. Dinner still late on most days.
O: BP 124/80 mmHg, pulse 76/min, wt 84 kg. O/E: NAD.
A: 1. T2DM, control worse this quarter.
P: 1. Glimepiride returned to 2 mg OD before breakfast from today. 2. Continue metformin 1000 mg BD. 3. HbA1c sent today.
Adv: Three regular meals a day; walk 30 min after dinner; cut sweet tea. R/V in 4 months.

memories.author: lab
memories.text: Lab report: HbA1c (glycated haemoglobin) 9.1 % (reference below 5.7 %). Sample: venous blood, Sunrise Family Clinic.

memories.author: D01
memories.text: Rx change: glimepiride 1 mg with the iftar meal (Ramadan dose) changed back to 2 mg OD before breakfast, from 2026-04-14. Metformin 1000 mg BD unchanged.

memories.author: D01
memories.text:
S: k/c/o T2DM. Works long hours at the restaurant. Dinner around 11 pm most nights. Often skips breakfast on busy days. Drinks sweet soda during service. No hypoglycaemia.
O: BP 126/82 mmHg, pulse 80/min, wt 84 kg. O/E: NAD.
A: 1. T2DM, HbA1c 8.9 %, slightly lower than April but still above target.
P: 1. Continue metformin 1000 mg BD. 2. Continue glimepiride 2 mg OD before breakfast. 3. Diet plan given: 3 regular meals a day; breakfast within 1 hour of waking; take glimepiride before breakfast; no sugary drinks. 4. HbA1c in 3 months.
Adv: Walk 30 min after dinner, 5 days a week; keep meals to fixed times. R/V in 3 months.

memories.author: lab
memories.text: Lab report: HbA1c (glycated haemoglobin) 8.9 % (reference below 5.7 %). Sample: venous blood, Sunrise Family Clinic.

memories.author: patient
memories.text: App message from patient: 'Doctor, I saw a 16:8 intermittent fasting video on YouTube and want to start it this week. I plan to eat only between 12 pm and 8 pm and skip breakfast, to lose weight and bring my sugar down. Is this okay with my tablets?'
